idea-plugin.name: Antitheft
idea-plugin.description:
Stop infostealers in plugins, AI agents and the programs they start from stealing your wallets and passwords, and see who opens your secrets.

Every plugin you install runs with the same access you have. One bad update is enough for a plugin to read your wallet, the passwords your browser saved, or the session that keeps you signed in. Antitheft works with the Antitheft app, which locks your vaults on the computer itself, and brings that protection inside the IDE.

  • Blocks plugins from your vaults. A plugin's own code is refused when it reaches for a wallet, a password store or a browser's saved logins.
  • Stops what they start. A program a plugin downloads and runs is stopped when it goes for your vaults.
  • Covers AI agents and everything the IDE runs. Coding agents and assistants, the terminal, run configurations, MCP servers and package install scripts are refused your vaults the same way, and the alert shows where it came from.
  • Names the plugin. Every alert says which plugin was behind it, so you can disable or uninstall it right from the alert.
  • Shows you what is protected. The Vaults tab lists the wallets, password managers and browsers Antitheft found, and which ones only their own app can open.

Antitheft locks crypto wallets, browser passwords and cookies, password managers, authenticator apps, your desktop keyring and messaging and cloud sync logins. What it finds depends on the apps on your computer. Every supported app.

Needs the Antitheft app installed and running on the same computer. The plugin talks only to it and sends nothing anywhere else.

Source and issues: github.com/kinnector/antitheft-extension.
